transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um... I hope I'm not wasting your time, I know you're very busy. It's probably a little silly, really, but... well, I came in because I just can’t seem to stop seeing this... this sagging, uneven spot right around my jaw and my neck. 

I know I shouldn't let it bother me, and folks are sweet and try to tell me it looks completely normal, but... I just feel like it’s the very first thing people notice when they look at me. Like when I'm at work helping the families and the nurses, or even just talking to people at church, I just feel like everyone sees it right away. Is that... does that make sense why I'd want to come in and talk to someone about that?
Is it only this spot on your jaw and neck that bothers you, or are there other parts of your body that you're also concerned about?

Oh, no, it's really just the jaw and the neck area. I mean, I know I'm forty-eight, and I'm perfectly fine with getting older—I promise I'm not trying to look like a teenager or anything! I really don't want you to think I'm terribly vain or obsessed with my looks, because I'm honestly not. 

It's just... it's really just this one specific spot that just looks so, well, so wrong to me. Everything else is just fine, I'm just an everyday person otherwise. I hope that doesn't sound too foolish to say. Is it... is it normal to just be so bothered by one single thing like that?
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking or touching the area around your jaw and neck?

Well, I suppose... maybe just a little bit? I try very hard not to make a big fuss over it, because I know it’s silly. But, um... I guess before I leave for work, or if I have a meeting, I do find myself going back to the bathroom mirror a few times. Just to fix my collar, or maybe arrange my hair around my neck so the sagging isn't quite so obvious. I just want to look professional and put-together for the families I help, you know? 

And... well, sometimes I might take a quick peek in my phone camera, too. Just to be absolutely sure it's covered. I hope that doesn't sound terribly obsessive. I don't mean to be. I even ask my daughter if it looks strange sometimes, which I know probably bothers her... and, to be perfectly honest, doing all that has made me run late more than once. I feel just awful about holding people up. Is that... do you think that's somewhat normal, to want to double-check things like that?
Has your concern about the appearance of your jaw and neck area affected your relationships or work performance?

Oh, well... I really do try my best not to let it get in the way, because I truly love my job and the people I work with. But... I suppose if I'm being completely honest, it might have affected things just a little bit. I hope you don't think I'm a bad employee for saying this, but... well, they've offered me a few chances to help lead our staff meetings, or take on some supervisory pieces, and I... I passed on them. I just couldn't stop worrying that if I was up at the front of the room, everyone would just be staring right at my face and my neck. And, um, I have gotten a tiny bit behind on my paperwork a few times, just because I get stuck in the mirror trying to make sure I look presentable before I go back out. 

And as for my friends... well, I’ve actually stopped going to some of my book club and walking club activities lately. It just... getting ready and trying to hide the sagging just feels like so much work sometimes, so it's easier to just stay home. I know that sounds awful, and I really know I should be more social. Do you think... is it understandable that I'd just want to avoid those situations when I'm feeling so self-conscious?
Do you ever find yourself thinking about this sagging spot when you're not in front of a mirror or getting ready to go out?

Oh, um... you know, I don't really think so. I haven't really noticed doing that, anyway. Once I'm out the door, I try very hard to just focus on my clients and my work. I really don't want to be the sort of person who just sits around dwelling on their appearance all day long, you know? 

So I try to keep my mind busy with other things. I suppose if I'm not near a mirror or getting dressed, it's not really something I'm actively thinking about... at least, I don't think it is. I hope that's an okay answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information, and I'd really hate for you to think I'm completely consumed by it. Is it normal to just kind of put it out of your mind once you're busy?
Do you ever engage in any repetitive behaviors, like excessive grooming or camouflaging, specifically to hide or improve the appearance of the sagging spot on your jaw and neck?

Oh... well, I suppose that goes back to what I was mentioning just a little bit earlier. I hope it's okay that I'm repeating myself? But yes, um... before I leave for work or if I have a meeting, I do find myself going back to the bathroom mirror quite a few times. Just to... you know, fix my collar and arrange my hair around my neck so it hides the sagging a bit better. 

And then I'll usually take another quick look in my phone camera, or sometimes ask my daughter if it looks strange before I walk out the door. I know I said that before, and I really do feel embarrassed admitting that doing all that has made me late more than once. I just want to make sure it's covered up so I look presentable for my clients. I try very hard not to be "excessive" about it, though, because I know that sounds like a bad thing. Does... does that answer your question properly?
Have you noticed any significant impact on your daily life or relationships due to your concerns about the sagging spot on your jaw and neck?

Oh, um... well, I know we kind of touched on this a moment ago, and I really hope you don't mind me bringing it up again. I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the details you need. But yes, I suppose it has affected things a little bit. 

Like I mentioned, I really love my job, but I did pass up a few chances to help lead our staff meetings or take on some supervisory tasks. I just... I couldn't stop worrying that if I was up front, everyone would be staring right at my face and neck. And, um, I have fallen a tiny bit behind on my paperwork a couple of times, just because I get stuck in the mirror trying to make sure I look presentable. I know that probably sounds like I'm not a very dedicated worker, but I promise I really do try my best.

And with my friends... I did stop going to some of my book club and walking club activities. It just feels like so much work to get ready and try to hide the sagging, so it's been easier to just stay home. I know I should be more social, and I feel awful admitting that I've been avoiding them. Do you think it makes sense that I'd just want to step back from things when I'm feeling that way? I just hope you don't think I'm completely letting my life fall apart over this.
Do you think the sagging spot on your jaw and neck is something that other people can actually see, or is it something that you're more aware of than others?

Oh... well, um... that's a really good question. I guess... I mean, I know my daughter and some of my friends have told me that it looks fine, or that they don't even see what I'm talking about. And I really try to believe them, I do. I don't want to seem like I'm calling them liars or anything. 

But... honestly? I just feel like it's so obvious. It's actually the main reason I decided to come in and talk to you. I just can't stop seeing this sagging, uneven spot around my jaw and neck. And even though people say it's normal, I just... I can't shake the feeling that it's the very first thing that the families I work with, or the nurses, or even the people at my church notice when they look at me. 

I know that probably sounds a bit silly, or maybe a little vain, and I really hope you don't think poorly of me for saying it. I just want to be honest with you so you have the right information. Does that... does that make sense? That I could know people say one thing, but still feel like everyone is staring at it?
Do you think that if you were to show a picture of yourself to someone who doesn't know you, they would immediately notice the sagging spot on your jaw and neck?

Oh, um... well, I know I'm probably repeating myself a bit, and I'm so sorry if I'm not giving you the exact answer you're looking for. But yes... I really do think they would. 

Like I was saying just a moment ago, that's exactly why I felt I needed to come in and talk to someone. I just... I can't stop seeing that sagging, uneven spot right there on my jaw and neck. And I know I mentioned that my friends and family say it's fine, and I really try to listen to them. I don't want to seem ungrateful for their reassurance. But if a stranger were to look at a picture of me, I just... I truly feel like that sagging spot would be the very first thing they'd see. Just like I feel it's the first thing the families at work or the people at my church notice. 

I know it probably sounds like I'm making a mountain out of a molehill, and I really don't want you to think I'm just being overly dramatic. I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right. Do you think it's normal to worry that a stranger would see it just as clearly as I do?
Have you considered seeking cosmetic surgery or other medical treatments to fix the sagging spot on your jaw and neck?

Oh, um... surgery? No, I haven't really looked into anything like that. I know some people get things done, and I don't judge them at all, but I haven't actually gone to see a plastic surgeon or anything like that. 

I mean, I've bought some firming creams at the drugstore, just to see if they might help a little bit. I hope that doesn't sound too silly. But as for actual medical procedures or surgery, no, I haven't pursued that. I wouldn't want to do anything drastic, you know? Does that seem like the right approach to you, just trying to handle it on my own without going to those extremes?
Do you think the sagging spot on your jaw and neck is actually there, or is it something you're just perceiving?

Oh, um... well, I know I'm probably sounding like a broken record, and I'm so sorry to keep repeating myself. I hope I'm not being difficult. But... I really do believe it's actually there. 

I mean, like I mentioned earlier, that's the whole reason I came in to see you today. I just can't stop seeing that sagging, uneven spot. And I know folks tell me it looks normal, and I really, truly try to believe them, but... to me, it's just so real. I still feel like it's the very first thing the families I work with, or the nurses, or the people at church notice when they look at me. 

I hope you don't think I'm losing my mind or being stubborn about it. I know you're the professional and you might see it differently, but when I look in the mirror, I just see it so clearly. Is it okay that I feel that way? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the most honest answer I can.
Do you think your concern about the sagging spot on your jaw and neck is an exaggerated worry or a realistic concern?

Oh, um... gosh, I'm not exactly sure how to answer that. I'm sorry, I wish I had a more straightforward answer for you. I hope I'm not being frustrating. 

I mean... to me, it feels very realistic. When I'm getting ready for work or when I'm out, it just feels like this glaring thing. But... well, I guess since I'm sitting here talking to you about it, and since my family says I look fine... maybe it is an exaggerated worry? I really don't want to come across as vain or obsessed with myself, I promise I'm not like that. I just... I don't really know for sure where the line is between a normal worry and an exaggerated one. 

Does that make sense? I hope it's alright that I'm not totally sure. What do you think... does it sound to you like I'm exaggerating? I really value your opinion on this.
Have you avoided any important life events or activities because of your concern about the sagging spot on your jaw and neck?

Oh, um... well, I wouldn't say I've avoided anything *really* important, like family weddings or anything major like that. I always try to be there for the big things, I promise. I don't want to let anyone down. 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, and I hope this doesn't sound terrible... I have stepped back a little bit at work. Just minor things. Like, they asked me if I wanted to help lead some of our staff meetings or take on a few supervisory duties, and I... I passed on it. I just kept thinking about standing up there and having everyone staring at my face and my neck, and it just made me so anxious. And sometimes I get a little behind on my paperwork because I get stuck in the bathroom trying to fix my hair or my scarf so I look presentable before I can go out and do my job. I really try not to let it affect my work, though, I really do. 

And, um, socially... I guess I have missed a few things. I used to go to this book club and a walking group, and lately, I just... I haven't been going as much. Getting ready to go out just feels so exhausting sometimes, trying to hide everything. I just stay home instead. 

Does that sound really bad? I know I shouldn't let it get in the way of my life, and I'm trying to be better about it. I hope you don't think I'm just being lazy or avoiding my responsibilities. Is it somewhat normal for people to feel overwhelmed like that sometimes?
Do you feel like your concern about the sagging spot on your jaw and neck is causing you a lot of emotional pain or distress?

Oh, um... well, I wouldn't say it's causing me a *lot* of pain. I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I'm falling apart or anything like that. I know there are people dealing with much worse things, and I really try to keep things in perspective. I hope I don't sound like I'm complaining too much.

But... I guess it does bother me more than I'd like to admit. It just kind of weighs on me, you know? Like this constant, quiet hum in the back of my mind. It makes me feel a little down sometimes, just wishing I didn't look this way and wishing I didn't care so much about it. It's more of a... a frustration, I suppose, than actual distress. I really try to stay positive and keep a smile on my face for the people I take care of. 

Do you think that's a normal amount of distress to feel about something like this? I just want to make sure I'm not overreacting or making a bigger deal out of it than I should be. I'm really trying my best to handle it well.
Is your concern about your appearance limited to this one area around your jaw and neck, or do you sometimes worry about other aspects of how you look?

Oh, um... no, it's really just this one spot. Just the jaw and the neck area. I mean, I know I'm getting older and things naturally change, and I'm honestly okay with the rest of me! I really try not to be, you know, overly focused on my looks in general. I hope you don't think I spend all day scrutinizing every little thing in the mirror, because I really don't. 

It's just... for some reason, it's only this one specific area that I just can't seem to stop worrying about. Everything else is completely fine. Does that make sense? Is it pretty common for people to just have one single thing that bothers them like that? I'm hoping that means it's not too serious, right? I really want to make sure I'm keeping a healthy perspective on all of this.
Do you feel a strong urge to perform specific rituals or behaviors to temporarily reduce your anxiety about the sagging spot on your jaw and neck?

Oh, um... well, I wouldn't call them *rituals*, exactly. That sounds a little extreme, like something you'd see on TV, right? I really try not to let it get to that point. I just... I like to make sure I look neat and professional before I head out. I think anyone working in personal care wants to present a good image for their clients, you know?

But... I guess I do have a bit of a routine. Before I leave for work, or if I have to go to a meeting, I... well, I do find myself going back to the bathroom mirror a few times. Just to double-check. I'll adjust my collar, or try to arrange my hair around my neck so it falls just right. And sometimes, just to be absolutely sure, I'll take a quick look in my phone camera. It's just a little habit to help me feel more put together. 

And, um, occasionally I might ask my daughter if it looks okay, or if it looks strange. I don't want to bother her too much with it, but sometimes I just need a little reassurance. I will admit, doing all of that... it has made me run late a couple of times. Not terribly late! Just a few minutes here and there. 

Is it okay to have little habits like that to help you feel more comfortable? I really hope it doesn't sound like I'm obsessing over it. I'm just trying to manage it the best way I know how.
Do you think there's any possibility that the sagging spot on your jaw and neck might not be as noticeable to others as it is to you?

Oh, um... well, I guess I'm not entirely sure. I really try to tell myself that people aren't staring at it. I mean, I certainly hope they aren't! I'd hate to think my clients are distracted by it when I'm supposed to be taking care of them, you know? I always want to make sure I'm a positive, pleasant presence for the people I work with. 

But... when I look in the mirror, it just seems so clear to me. It's hard to imagine that other people don't see exactly what I'm seeing. But honestly, I don't really know. People are usually very polite, so even if it was really noticeable, I don't think they'd say anything to my face. 

I really do try to be rational about it, though. Do you think it's possible that I'm just being my own worst critic? I really hope that's all it is. I want to be sensible about this and not make a mountain out of a molehill. Does that sound like a healthy way to look at it? I just want to make sure I'm thinking about this the right way.
Do you think it's possible that the sagging spot on your jaw and neck doesn't actually look as bad to others as it does to you?

Oh, um... isn't that sort of what you just asked? I'm sorry, I don't mean to be difficult, I just... I want to make sure I'm understanding you correctly. 

But, yes, I... I suppose it's possible. Like I said, I really try to tell myself that it's not as glaring to everyone else as it is to me. I mean, I certainly hope it isn't! I'd feel just awful if I was making people uncomfortable. 

I guess I just... I really want to believe that it's mostly in my head, or that I'm just being too hard on myself. That's a good way to look at it, right? I'm really trying my best to keep a positive attitude about the whole thing. I hope I'm answering your questions okay... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you think your perception of the sagging spot on your jaw and neck might be different from how it actually looks?

Oh my... I feel terrible, I must be doing a really bad job of explaining myself since we keep coming back to this. I'm so sorry if I'm not giving you the right answer! I really am trying to be helpful. 

To be completely honest, I just don't know for sure. When I look in the mirror, the sagging just looks so obvious to me. But... well, you're the expert, right? If you think my eyes are sort of... exaggerating it, or that I'm seeing it differently than it really is, I'm more than willing to believe you. I really want to be sensible about all of this and follow your lead. 

I would actually be so relieved if it turned out I was just seeing things worse than they are. That would be a good thing, wouldn't it? I hope I'm making sense now... I just want to make sure I'm being a good patient and giving you what you need to help me.
